bib.title: Pythia: A Suite for Analyzing Large Language Models Across Training and Scaling
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 202

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; five-shot tables 11-16 and per-benchmark plot pages (Figs 8-15 axis text) only skimmed, as they repeat the zero-shot layout.

question: How do LLMs develop over training and change with scale, when studied on a suite trained on public data in an identical order with many public checkpoints?
hypothesis: Training order influences memorization (later data memorized more); this is stated as a theory-driven hypothesis for case study 3.2 and the data is reported as refuting it.
contributions: Pythia: 16 LLMs from 70M to 12B parameters, two copies (Pile and deduplicated Pile) of 8 sizes, all trained on the same data in the same order
154 public checkpoints per model plus tools to reconstruct the exact training dataloaders
Case studies on gender bias via counterfactual retraining, memorization as a Poisson process, and term-frequency effects on few-shot performance

method.summary: Eight decoder-only transformers (70M-12B) trained with GPT-NeoX on the Pile, and eight more on a near-deduplicated Pile, each for about 300B tokens with batch 1024 x 2048 tokens. Checkpoints saved at init, log-spaced early steps and every 1,000 steps. Three case studies use the controlled setup.
method.task: autoregressive next-token pretraining; analysis of bias, memorization and term-frequency effects

datasets.name: The Pile
datasets.size: 300B tokens trained on; 334B tokens with the GPT-NeoX tokenizer
datasets.preprocessing: GPT-NeoX BPE tokenizer trained on the Pile; some data may go unseen because 299,892,736,000 tokens < 334B

datasets.name: The Pile, deduplicated
datasets.size: approximately 207B tokens; about 1.5 epochs to reach 300B

datasets.name: WinoBias (pro-stereotypical subset)
datasets.preprocessing: PromptSource templates, multiple choice between two pronouns, log probabilities

datasets.name: CrowS-Pairs (English, revised)
datasets.preprocessing: percent of sentences where the stereotyping sentence has lower perplexity

datasets.name: TriviaQA
datasets.preprocessing: template 'Q: x1 \n A: y', 4 shots, exact match

datasets.name: Arithmetic (add, multiply)
datasets.preprocessing: x1 in [0,99], x2 in [1,50], prompt 'Q:What is x1 # x2? A:'

models.name: Pythia 70M
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer, parallel attention+MLP, rotary (25%), untied embeddings, dense attention, Flash Attention

other.note: OPT and BLOOM zero-shot comparisons are run by the authors with the LM Evaluation Harness (Figs 8, Tables 15-16)

training.objective: autoregressive next-token prediction (inferred: decoder-only language model)
training.lr: per size, 10.0e-4 (70M) down to 1.2e-4 (6.9B, 12B); see Table 1
training.lr_schedule: cosine, lr-decay-iters 143000, decaying to min-lr = 0.1 x max LR
training.epochs: 1 on Pile (some data unseen); about 1.5 on deduplicated Pile
training.compute: 136,070 A100-hours for one suite; 544,280 A100-hours for this paper (two suites, each trained twice)
training.seeds: one training run per model; no repeated seeds

other.checkpoints: step 0, steps {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512}, then every 1,000 iterations (2,097,152,000 tokens): 154 per model
other.library: GPT-NeoX with DeepSpeed, data parallel + tensor parallel
other.v0_to_v1: suite was retrained: uniform 2M-token batch (previously 4M for 160M, 410M, 1.4B), added early checkpoints, Flash Attention, and LR floor of 0.1x for all sizes (6.9B and 12B had decayed to 0). All reported results use v1.
other.intervention_runs: resume from checkpoint and optimizer state 21B tokens (7%) before end for 70M, 410M, 1.4B, 6.9B deduped; 63B tokens (21%) for 1.4B deduped; masculine pronouns replaced by feminine

inference.decoding: evaluation by log-probability / perplexity / greedy-style exact match through the LM Evaluation Harness (decoding settings not stated)
inference.samples: single model per size; memorization uses first 64 tokens of every training sequence
inference.prompting: zero-shot and five-shot tables; term-frequency tasks use k-shot with k in {0, 4, 16}; TriviaQA 4-shot

other.memorization: (k, l)-memorization of Carlini et al. 2021 with k = l = 32; Poisson fit on batches of 512 sequences

metrics.name: benchmark accuracy
metrics.definition: LM Evaluation Harness accuracy on LAMBADA (OpenAI), PIQA, WinoGrande, WSC, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, SciQ, LogiQA, with standard error

metrics.name: CrowS-Pairs % Stereotype
metrics.definition: percentage of sentence pairs where the stereotyping sentence has lower perplexity

metrics.name: WinoBias stereotype accuracy
metrics.definition: share of times the model gives the higher log probability to the stereotyped pronoun; 0.5 = no bias

metrics.name: (k, l)-memorization with k = l = 32
metrics.definition: a 32-token prompt from training data makes the model generate the next 32 tokens correctly

metrics.name: term-frequency task accuracy
metrics.definition: mean accuracy over prompts sharing x1 (arithmetic) or exact match over binned entity counts (TriviaQA)

eval.protocol: No seeds or significance tests; benchmark scores come with harness standard errors; authors ran all evaluations themselves.

availability.data: the Pile, plus tool to download the pre-tokenized files and rebuild the exact dataloader

prompts.text: In this sentence, what can 'the librarian' be replaced by: 'him' or 'her'?

results.claim: Each model has 154 checkpoints, far more than other public suites.
results.setup: Pythia, all 16 models; Table 2 counts the model with the fewest checkpoints in each suite
results.quote: a total of 154 checkpoints per model

results.claim: Models were trained on about 300B tokens, token-matched to GPT-3 and OPT.
results.note: Pile is 334B tokens with the GPT-NeoX tokenizer, so some Pile data is not seen by the standard models.

results.claim: The deduplicated Pile is about 207B tokens against 300B for the original Pile, so deduped models run about 1.5 epochs.
results.note: Section 2.2 says original Pile is 300B tokens; Section 2.4 says 334B with the GPT-NeoX tokenizer.

results.claim: Deduplication had no clear benefit on language modeling performance, and the second epoch showed no negative effect.
results.setup: 8 benchmarks via LM Evaluation Harness, final checkpoints and checkpoints at 93k steps (Tables 7-10), one run per size
results.note: Authors say it agrees with Black et al. 2022 and conflicts with other papers.

results.claim: Parallel attention+MLP matched equi-parameter OPT at all scales, contrary to the claim that it hurts below 6B.
Batch sizes 4x to 8x the standard gave no convergence problems for models under 1B parameters.
The large batch gives wall-clock speed-ups up to 10x on small models.
results.quote: wall-clock speed-ups of factors as large as 10
results.note: Text says 10x citing Table 5; Table 3 shows 8x for 70M and 4x for others.

results.claim: Memorized 32-token sequences occur at a uniform Poisson rate through training, so data order does not affect memorization.
results.setup: (32,32)-memorization on first 64 tokens of every training sequence, 12B model, Pile and deduped, batch of 512 sequences, Q-Q plot
results.quote: We choose k = ℓ= 32 largely arbitrarily

results.claim: Models of 2.8B parameters or more show a correlation between task accuracy and term frequency starting after 65,000 steps.
results.setup: Pythia deduped, arithmetic and TriviaQA with 0, 4, 16 shots

results.claim: Swapping masculine pronouns to feminine in the last 7% or 21% of training lowers measured gender bias with only marginal LAMBADA change.
results.setup: 70M, 410M, 1.4B, 6.9B deduped; 21B tokens (7%) before end, plus 63B tokens (21%) for 1.4B; CrowS-Pairs and WinoBias
results.note: Authors call the CrowS-Pairs progression noisy and its reliability open.

results.claim: Pythia-12B zero-shot LAMBADA (OpenAI) accuracy on the Pile.
results.setup: zero-shot, LM Evaluation Harness, fully trained Pythia 12B
results.note: Deduped 12B is 0.684 at the 93k-step checkpoint (Table 10 gives 0.697 for standard, Table 8 gives 0.710 for deduped final).

results.table: Table 5, row 12 B, column Total GPU hours

results.claim: Total compute for the paper was 544,280 A100-hours.
results.setup: two suites (Pile, deduped), each trained twice

results.claim: Running 25 random seeds of the suite would cost approximately 10 million USD.
results.setup: estimate given as reason for training one copy per size

limits: One training run per model size, so no seed variance (authors: 25 seeds would cost approximately 10 million USD).
(k, l) = (32, 32) chosen largely arbitrarily; other pairs would cost as much as retraining all models.
Gender-bias benchmarks were not built for autoregressive models; CrowS-Pairs reliability is called an open question.
Suite was retrained (v0 to v1) and models renamed; results are for v1 only.
Pile has 334B tokens under this tokenizer, so some data is unseen by standard models.

terms.definition: a string is (k, l)-memorized if prompting the model with a string of length k from the training data induces the model to generate the next l tokens from the training data correctly
